summary: Sanders County, MT pole L-4 tower in the Kootenai NF; firelookout.com dates it 1935 but 1936 items show construction, and it was destroyed in 1963. No site description.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1963 per firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page; the Montana list also marks it gone

events.note: firelookout.com gives 1935 as the build year; 1936 newspaper items disagree (see resolved_conflicts)
September 1936 newspaper item: crew packing equipment for a new lookout at the head of Graves Creek; Ben Cox foreman in charge
June 1946: Forest Service packers found the lookout station wrecked after a bear got into the lookout
Destroyed in 1963 per firelookout.com; the Forest Lookouts page gives the same year and cites Kresek

evidence.supports: pole L-4 tower built in 1935 and destroyed in 1963
evidence.quote: This 10' pole L-4 tower, built in 1935, was destroyed in 1963.

evidence.supports: the packing item is dated September 2, 1936
crew packing equipment for a new lookout at the head of Graves Creek
evidence.quote: They are packing equipment for a new lookout on Vermilion peak at the head of Graves creek.

evidence.supports: Ben Cox as foreman in charge
evidence.quote: Ben Cox is the foreman in charge.

evidence.supports: the June 1946 item is dated June 22, 1946
June 1946 packers found the station wrecked
evidence.quote: Forest service packers, arriving at Vermillion Lookout station, found the place a wreck.

evidence.supports: a bear got up the tower and into the lookout
evidence.quote: bruin managed to get up there and into the lookout itself.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1935 for the pole L-4 tower; the Forest Lookouts page quotes September 1936 items about packing equipment for a new lookout and a crew building one. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com gives the tower as '10' pole L-4 tower'; a 10-foot height looks wrong for a lookout tower, so no height is recorded. The build year (1935) disagrees with the 1936 newspaper items. The 1963 destruction date is cited by the Forest Lookouts page to a source named Kresek, which we did not see. The 1946 entry concerns packers and a bear, not lookout staff, so no staffing event is recorded. The 1936 item spells the peak 'Vermilion'. No source describes the site or access today. Brief agency and county agree with the sources; no corrections.
